before.title: 9-Speed Automatic Harsh / Jerky Shifting and Acceleration Hesitation
before.description: The Jatco 9-speed automatic in the Z draws owner complaints of hesitation/lag from a stop, jerking or a forward thump when decelerating to a stop, and abrupt low-speed gear changes. The behavior parallels documented shift-quality issues on the same transmission family in the Frontier/Titan/Pathfinder, which received TSBs for hesitation and shift shock. Some owners report the NISMO variant is less affected.
before.solution: Dealers typically address shift-quality complaints with TCM reprogramming/software updates; a transmission fluid service can help in some cases. Persistent harsh shifting should be documented for warranty repair.
symptoms: Hesitation or lag when accelerating from a stop
Jerking, lurching, or a thump at low speed / when coming to a stop
Hard or abrupt downshifts

before.title: Heat Soak Triggers Timing Pull / Power Reduction at High Oil Temps
before.description: Under hard or track driving in hot conditions the RZ34 is prone to heat soak: the factory air-to-water charge cooler saturates and the ECU pulls timing, reducing power, with brief limp/power-reduction reported as oil temps climb toward roughly 270°F. The condition resolves once temperatures drop. Owners view factory cooling as marginal for sustained high-performance use, though Nissan reportedly improved it relative to the Q50/Q60.
before.solution: Add an auxiliary oil cooler and an upgraded intercooler/heat exchanger, allow cool-down between hard pulls, and keep tunes conservative to limit heat-induced timing pull. Aftermarket cooling upgrades are the common owner remedy.
symptoms: Power loss after repeated hard pulls or track laps
Brief power reduction / limp behavior when oil temperature gets high
Power returns once the engine cools
Worse performance in hot ambient temperatures

before.description: On 2023 Z models with the 9-speed Jatco automatic, resistance between the parking rod and wedge inside the transmission housing can keep the parking pawl from fully engaging, so the car can roll away even when shifted into Park with no warning. before.solution: Covered under NHTSA recall 22V-671. Dealers reprogram the Transmission Control Module (TCM) free of charge. Until repaired, owners were advised to always set the parking brake.

Car moves on an incline despite being in Park

before.title: Pop-Up Engine Hood May Not Deploy in Pedestrian Crash — Recalls 23V-725 & 24V-798
before.description: The Z's active pop-up hood pedestrian-protection system was subject to two recalls. In 23V-725, fasteners in the left-side front bumper reinforcement clip can loosen; in 24V-798, the right-side pedestrian-detection sensor connectors may be reversed in the front bumper harness due to a wiring-design drawing error. Either fault can prevent the hood from raising in a frontal pedestrian impact, increasing injury risk.
before.solution: Both are free dealer repairs. For 23V-725 dealers tighten the bumper reinforcement clip fasteners; for 24V-798 dealers replace the front bumper harness. Owners can verify open recalls by VIN at NHTSA.

before.title: Twin-Turbo Wastegate Rattle (VR30DDTT Engine)
before.description: The 2023+ Nissan Z uses the VR30DDTT 3.0L twin-turbo V6 (shared with Infiniti) which develops a wastegate rattle at idle and low RPM. before.solution: Dealer may replace turbocharger assembly under warranty if noise is excessive. Aftermarket turbo blankets can dampen the noise. Some tuners install external wastegate setups to eliminate the issue entirely. Cost if out of warranty: $2,000-4,000 per turbo.

before.title: VR30DDTT Oil Pressure Control Solenoid Failure Leading to Spun Rod Bearings
before.description: The twin-turbo VR30DDTT uses an oil pressure control (OPC) solenoid beside the oil pump that bleeds pressure at low load. If it sticks open, the bypass leak persists at all RPM and starves the bearings of oil, leading to spun rod bearings and catastrophic engine failure. There is no check-engine warning beforehand — only a red low-oil-pressure light once pressure is already critically low.
before.solution: Frequent oil changes with quality synthetic and oil-pressure monitoring reduce risk; some owners delete/block off the OPC solenoid preventively. A failure that damages bearings requires an engine rebuild or replacement (roughly $10,000-$15,000).
symptoms: Sudden low oil pressure (red oil light) with no prior warning
Rod-knock / knocking noise from the engine
Catastrophic engine failure, often reported between roughly 40,000-70,000 miles
Oil pressure dropping under load at high RPM
